text: More than 1,200 years ago, Vikings sailed out from Scandinavia: today’s Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
At home most people were farmers who kept cattle, sheep and pigs.
src: Scandinavian raiders, traders and settlers whose voyages between the 790s and the 1060s / Scandinavia, in present-day Denmark, Norway and Sweden
Most Scandinavians were free farmers who raised cattle, sheep, pigs, barley and oats

text: Their oak ships could cross the open sea and sail up shallow rivers.
Two women were buried with great honour in this ship, found at Oseberg in Norway.
src: Built of overlapping oak planks on a keel, light and flexible, with a square sail and oars, they could cross open sea, run up shallow rivers and land on beaches
Some were buried with great honour, like the two women laid in the Oseberg ship in 834 / The ship burials of Oseberg and Gokstad in Norway

text: Viking raiders attacked monasteries and towns in Britain and Ireland, and took captives as slaves.
Vikings were also traders, who dealt in furs, walrus ivory, amber and silver.
src: Their raids fell hardest on monasteries and towns in Britain, Ireland and Francia / thralls, slaves, many of them captives taken in raids
merchants who dealt in furs, walrus ivory, amber, slaves and silver

text: They settled Iceland and Greenland, and about 1,000 years ago some reached Newfoundland, in the Americas.
src: Norse farmers settled the Faroes, Iceland from about 870 and Greenland from about 985 under Erik the Red, and briefly reached Newfoundland / dated to the year 1021 ... the earliest exact year known for Europeans in the Americas

text: They believed in gods like Odin and Thor, until kings such as Harald Bluetooth became Christian.
src: the gods were many, among them Odin ... Thor / Harald Bluetooth, king of Denmark, accepted baptism around 965 and raised the great stone at Jelling, which says that he “made the Danes Christian”

text: A Viking leader, Rollo, was given lands around Rouen that became Normandy.
English words such as sky, egg, knife and window come from the Vikings’ language, Old Norse.
src: In 911 Charles the Simple granted the leader Rollo lands around Rouen, the origin of the Duchy of Normandy
English took from Old Norse everyday words such as sky, egg, knife, window, husband and law
